prompt.text:
In `solution.rs`, implement a standard-library-only parser for semicolon-separated application settings.

Expose:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ParseSettings {
    pub allow_missing_required: bool,
    pub reject_null_required: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AppProfile {
    pub endpoint: Option<String>,
    pub pool_size: u16,
    pub tracing: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ProfileError {
    Malformed { segment: usize },
    UnknownKey(String),
    DuplicateKey(String),
    MissingEndpoint,
    NullEndpoint,
    InvalidValue { key: String, value: String },
}

pub fn parse_profile(input: &str, settings: ParseSettings) -> Result<AppProfile, ProfileError>;
```

The grammar is zero or more `key=value` segments separated by `;`. Leading/trailing whitespace around segments, keys, and values is ignored. Empty segments are malformed. Keys are exactly `endpoint`, `pool_size`, and `tracing`; duplicates fail before value conversion. `endpoint=null` means no endpoint, while any other value, including the empty string, is stored literally after trimming. Missing endpoint fails unless `allow_missing_required`; an explicit null fails whenever `reject_null_required`, regardless of `allow_missing_required`. If allowed, missing or null endpoints become `None`. `pool_size` defaults to 12 and accepts decimal `u16` values from 1 through 1024. `tracing` defaults to false and accepts exactly `true` or `false`. For a wholly empty or whitespace-only input, treat all keys as missing rather than producing `Malformed`. Process segments left-to-right and return the first error. Provide a new implementation; do not include `main`.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
